\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بلبل} (bolbol)}{بلبل (bolbol)}]{\fa{بلبل} (bolbol) — a nightingale}

\label{lesson:FA-C209-bolbol}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for shade, then the Persian for temperature.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بلبل}}
\textbf{\fa{بلبل}} — \emph{bolbol} — \textquotedblleft{}a nightingale\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bolbol} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{bulbul}, \textquotedblleft{}nightingale\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), a name that imitates the bird's song.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گورخر} (gurekhar)}{گورخر (gurekhar)}]{\fa{گورخر} (gurekhar) — a zebra}

\label{lesson:FA-C209-gurekhar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a nightingale, then the Persian for a crocodile.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گورخر}}
\textbf{\fa{گورخر}} — \emph{gurekhar} — \textquotedblleft{}a zebra\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gurekhar} is \emph{gur}, \textquotedblleft{}wild ass, onager\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{khar}, \textquotedblleft{}donkey\textquotedblright{}: the striped wild donkey. Both are native Persian; \emph{khar} is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{xar}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بره} (bare)}{بره (bare)}]{\fa{بره} (bare) — a lamb}

\label{lesson:FA-C209-bare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a crocodile, then the Persian for a zebra.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بره}}
\textbf{\fa{بره}} — \emph{bare} — \textquotedblleft{}a lamb\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bare} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{warrag}, \textquotedblleft{}lamb\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB takes it back to an Indo-European word for a ram or lamb, the word behind Greek \emph{arēn}, \textquotedblleft{}lamb\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خرچنگ} (kharchang)}{خرچنگ (kharchang)}]{\fa{خرچنگ} (kharchang) — a crab}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خرچنگ}}
\textbf{\fa{خرچنگ}} — \emph{kharchang} — \textquotedblleft{}a crab\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kharchang} is usually explained as built from \emph{khar}, \textquotedblleft{}big, coarse\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{chang}, \textquotedblleft{}claw\textquotedblright{}: the big-clawed creature.
\end{cousinweb}
